newsitem.title: USA: Pan Am to acquire Carnival Air Lines.
newsitem.headline: Pan Am to acquire Carnival Air Lines.

text.p: Pan American World Airways said Friday it had reached a definitive agreement to acquire Carnival Air Lines.
Carnival Air, formed in 1988, operates a fleet of 27 jet aircraft between South Florida, the Northeast, California and the Caribbean.
It had about $270 million in revenues in 1996. It is majority owned by Micky Arison, who is chairman and chief executive of Carnival Corp, which operates Carnival Cruse Lines.
The value of the transaction was not specified by PanAm.
PanAm said that the agreement provides that, assuming assuming certain conditions are met, Micky Arison, Carnival's primary shareholder, will make a $30 million capital investment.
As a result, Arison would hold approximately 9.5 million shares of Pan Am stock which would constitute approximately 42 percent of the outstanding shares of Pan Am stock, it said.
Last July, PanAm agreed to pay about $100 million for Carnival Air but the deal was called off after PanAm examined the carrier's books and sought to rework the terms.

Pan Am said it has arranged for a private placement of up to $30 million in a new series of convertible preferred stock. It said the financing, when combined with the additional investment from Arison, will provide Pan Am with some $60 million in additional liquidity.

"The Carnival Air acquisition elevates Pan Am to a stronger competitive position and provides significant benefits of critical mass in an expedited, yet controlled manner," said Martin R. Shugrue Jr, Pan Am's president and chief executive officer.

"We were earlier attracted to Carnival Air by its excellent route system, modern fleet and experienced work force and now believe even more fervently that the well-known Pan Am brand, coupled with Carnival Air's substantial assets, will result in a world-class airline," he added.

Commenting on the proposed acquisition, Arison said, "We are proud of the accomplishments of Carnival Air Lines and are confident that its future value will be greatly enhanced in combination with Pan Am which has demonstrated its commitment to providing top-quality service to the traveling public.

Pan Am has four A300's with two more to be delivered in the next two months. It currently flies between New York and Los Angeles, New York and Miami, New York and San Juan, and between Miami and Chicago, as well as Miami and San Juan.
The airline has announced that it will begin service between New York and Santo Domingo on April 6.
